#### 1. Omenn syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.785)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:17642)

**Proposed mechanism:** RAG2 pathogenic variant in MONDO:0011225 (HGNC:17642) —DISRUPTS→ RAG2 (HGNC:17642); RAG2 (HGNC:17642) —DISRUPTS→ V(D)J recombination (REACT:R-HSA-168774); V(D)J recombination (REACT:R-HSA-168774) —DISRUPTS→ T cell development (REACT:R-HSA-168774); T cell development (REACT:R-HSA-168774) —LEADS_TO→ Immune dysfunction in MONDO:0011225 (HP:0002715); RAG2 pathogenic variant in Omenn syndrome (HGNC:17642) —DISRUPTS→ RAG2 (HGNC:17642); RAG2 (HGNC:17642) —DISRUPTS→ V(D)J recombination (REACT:R-HSA-168774); V(D)J recombination (REACT:R-HSA-168774) —DISRUPTS→ T cell development (REACT:R-HSA-168774); T cell development (REACT:R-HSA-168774) —LEADS_TO→ Immune dysfunction in Omenn syndrome (HP:0002715). Loss-of-function mutations in RAG2 impair V(D)J recombination, which is essential for T cell receptor and B cell receptor gene rearrangement. This disruption leads to severe combined immunodeficiency and autoimmune features in both MONDO:0011225 and Omenn syndrome, with Omenn syndrome representing a more severe allelic form.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of functionally distinct pathogenic variants in RAG2 that cause loss-of-function in MONDO:0011225 but gain-of-function or a different mechanistic impact in Omenn syndrome. _(variant: Exclusion of pathogenic variants in RAG2 with a population frequency >0.01 in relevant gnomAD populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in RAG2 allows for potential therapeutic strategies targeting immune reconstitution or modulation in both conditions. Gene therapy approaches aimed at restoring RAG2 function could be a unified treatment strategy.

Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in H4C3 also disrupt DNA repair, leading to global developmental delay. The convergence is on the shared critical pathway of DNA repair.

**How to falsify it:** The hypothesis would be falsified if mutations in DCLRE1C or H4C3 were found to have no impact on DNA repair, or if the identified neurodevelopmental phenotypes could be definitively attributed to entirely separate molecular pathways in both diseases. _(variant: Absence of pathogenic variants in gnomAD for the identified causal variants in DCLRE1C and H4C3 would weaken the genetic evidence.)_
